title: Uterine fibroids by layer
claims: FIGO classification is by position relative to the endometrial cavity and serosa: 0-2 submucosal, 3-4 intramural, 5-7 subserosal (8 = other, e.g. cervical).
FIGO 0: pedunculated, intracavitary. FIGO 1: submucosal, <50% intramural. FIGO 2: submucosal, ≥50% intramural.
FIGO 3: intramural, touches the endometrium. FIGO 4: intramural, no contact with the endometrium.
FIGO 5: subserosal, ≥50% intramural. FIGO 6: subserosal, <50% intramural. FIGO 7: pedunculated subserosal.
Submucosal fibroids distort the cavity: heavy menstrual bleeding, anemia, infertility, recurrent pregnancy loss.
Hysteroscopic resection is an option for FIGO types 0-2.
Intramural fibroids enlarge the uterus: bulk symptoms, heavy or prolonged bleeding, pain.
Type 3 touches the endometrium and can behave like a submucosal lesion.
Subserosal fibroids bulge outward: pelvic pressure, urinary frequency (bladder), constipation; less often abnormal bleeding.
A pedunculated subserosal fibroid (FIGO 7) can torse, causing acute pain. Red degeneration is more common in pregnancy.
